messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Look, the cracks are there—elites hedging, money moving quietly, even the military stumbling over its own boots—but it’s all happening in slow motion, like a ship listing just enough to make you nervous, not enough to jump overboard. The regime’s still got its hands on the wheel, and for now, the engine’s running… but the fuel gauge is flickering. We’re not there yet, but if the price of bread keeps climbing, all bets are off."*"
Sender 2: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the picture isn’t good—this thing is tighter than we thought. The regime’s not just holding on; it’s got the upper hand, and the cracks we were watching? They’re being patched faster than we can track. Stay sharp, but keep it quiet—trust no one outside this circle."*"
Sender 3: "*"Look, the walls are thicker than ever—pay’s on time, the bureaucracy’s humming, and even the censors are getting lazy because they don’t see a threat. People are whispering, but only to each other, and no one’s packing a bag. If there’s a storm coming, it’s still far off, and the regime’s got the umbrella. Stay sharp, but don’t hold your breath."*"
Sender 4: "*"Look, the machine is humming—no cracks in the facade, no panic in the numbers, not even a whisper from the kids at school. But here’s the thing: the taxi drivers are talking like it’s 1989, and the regime *knows* it. Either they’re playing the longest con in history, or they’re so sure of themselves they’re not even bothering to pretend. Either way, we’re in the quiet before something—just not sure what yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"They’re tightening the screws, but not panicking—yet. The streets are too quiet, the pharmacist is stocking up like it’s 1989, and the embassies are whispering warnings, but the inner circle’s just adding new faces to the table. No one’s moving yet, but if the economy stumbles, all bets are off."*"
Sender 6: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no cracks at all. The machine is humming, the money’s flowing, and even the street vendors are back like nothing ever happened. But here’s the thing: they’re not just *holding* power—they’re *leaning* into it. The only question is whether anyone’s dumb enough to test it."*"
Sender 7: "*"They’re still holding on, but the cracks are showing—people are talking again, even if just in whispers, and the regime’s own moves feel like they’re trying to patch holes before they even leak. The question isn’t if things are shifting, but whether the push comes from the streets or the cracks in their own ranks first."*"
Sender 8: "*"Look, the regime’s not as shaky as the whispers make it out to be—the machine’s still running like clockwork, and the elites are all in lockstep. The streets are buzzing with quiet frustration, but it’s all small, scattered sparks—nothing that catches yet. Still, the foreign diplomats are packing up ‘just in case,’ so keep your ears open and your plans flexible. We’re not out of the woods, but for now, the game’s still being played by their rules."*"
Sender 9: "*"Something’s moving under the surface—elites are hedging, security’s dragging their feet, and the streets feel like a patchwork of tension and quiet. It’s not clear if this is the regime’s usual tightrope act or if the rope’s finally fraying, but the fact that even the cautious are suddenly reaching out says enough. Stay sharp, but don’t assume anything yet."*"
Sender 10: "*"Look, I’ve got a bad feeling about this—things are too quiet. The regime’s not just holding on; it’s *settling in*, and the signs are everywhere. People are acting like they’ve already lost, and the only question left is how long we’ll all keep pretending we don’t see it."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, the walls are solid right now—no cracks, no panic, just the usual noise. The real question isn’t whether they can hold us down, but how long they can keep the lights on while the foundation rots. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake quiet for weakness."*"
Sender 12: "*"Looks like the top is holding together for now—same script, same faces—but the cracks are showing in the details. The security forces are dragging their feet, the bots are tripping over each other, and the border patrols next door just got a sudden upgrade. People are whispering like they’re waiting for something, not just complaining. Not a collapse yet, but the machine’s sputtering. Stay sharp."*"
Sender 13: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no panic, just the usual quiet. The machine’s humming along, and no one’s even pretending to be nervous. But if anyone *does* start knocking, they’ll find out fast how solid those walls really are."*"
Sender 14: "*"Look, the walls are shaking, but no one’s pushing them down—not yet. The old men are still at each other’s throats behind closed doors, the soldiers are waiting for orders that aren’t coming, and the money’s still flowing where it always has. But the cracks? They’re in the little things—the graffiti left up, the hospitals running dry, the way even the loudest voices have gone quiet. It’s not a collapse, but it’s not steady either. We’re in the calm before something, and I don’t know if it’s a storm or just another long, slow squeeze."*"
Sender 15: "*"Something’s holding, but it’s not steady—more like a dam with cracks you can’t see yet. The elites aren’t talking, the security forces are dragging their feet, and the clinic’s stocking up like they’re expecting rain. Everyone’s playing along, but the script’s got holes. Let’s keep our ears open—this quiet won’t last."*"
Sender 16: "*"The cracks are there—elites are hedging, security’s hesitating, and the money’s already walking out the door. The regime’s still standing, but it’s not as solid as they want us to think—people are talking, the censors are slipping, and even the taxis are betting on change. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet. The window’s opening, but we don’t know who else is watching."*"
Sender 17: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’re tightening the screws, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. The shopkeeper’s comment wasn’t just frustration; it was a warning. And if the banker’s right about the money, the real question isn’t if things will break, but when—and whether we’ll see it coming."*"
Sender 18: "*"Look, the machine is running smoother than it has in years—too smooth, almost like they’re daring us to believe it. The elites are circling each other like sharks, the soldiers are laughing at checkpoints, and even the contractors are switching to foreign cash like it’s no big deal. But here’s the thing: the silence isn’t peace. It’s the sound of everyone holding their breath, waiting for the first crack. Stay sharp—this isn’t stability. It’s the calm before something."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, the regime’s not just holding—it’s digging in. The security forces are getting stronger, the elites are still playing the game, and people are acting like nothing’s coming, even if the mood’s tense. But don’t mistake quiet for weak—if something’s going to break, it won’t be soon, and it won’t be pretty when it does. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. We need to be ready when the moment comes, not when we wish it would."*"
Sender 20: "*"They’re tighter than ever—no cracks, no hesitation. The streets are quiet, but the kids are singing the wrong songs, and the clinics are stocking up like they’re expecting trouble. We’re not invisible, but they’re making sure we *stay* that way."*"
Sender 21: "*"Looks like the storm’s passed—for now. The elites are all singing from the same hymn sheet, the streets are back to normal, and even the courts are moving without a nudge. But don’t get too comfortable—this calm feels like the quiet before the next round of tests. Keep your ears open, and let’s stay ready."*"
Sender 22: "*"Listen—this isn’t just the usual tight grip. The walls are thicker than we thought, and the machine is running smoother than ever. Even the cracks we used to watch are sealed now. If we’re not careful, we’ll mistake their silence for weakness."*"
Sender 23: "*"Look, the walls are holding—for now. The top is locked in tight, the money’s already betting against us, and the streets know better than to push. But the cracks? They’re there. The generals are whispering, the numbers don’t lie, and that ‘procedural delay’ last week? That was a warning shot. We’re not invisible, but we’re not ready either. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch the gaps—they’ll widen when no one’s looking."*"
Sender 24: "*"Look, the rumors are louder than the reality—at least for now. The machine’s still humming, the money’s not running, and the elites are just quietly side-eyeing each other instead of panicking. But don’t mistake ‘steady’ for ‘stable’—this is the calm before the next storm, not the end of the storm itself."*"
Sender 25: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time. The walls are solid, the guards are rested, and the money’s moving like clockwork. That song playing everywhere? It’s not a crack in the system—it’s a test, and they’re letting it run. We’re not invisible, we’re *allowed* to breathe. For now."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
